source_snapshot.title: fix(ingest): resolve PHP calls through typed receivers
source_snapshot.body:
Fixes #381.

## Summary
Resolve PHP member calls through declared receiver types and keep those targets stable across incremental maps.

## Type
- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Test
- [ ] CI

## Changes
- Capture receivers for regular and nullsafe PHP member calls.
- Resolve constructor-promoted properties, typed properties, typed parameters, and `$this` calls to qualified method names.
- Normalize PHP namespace imports to their imported class names.
- Pre-index PHP definitions for cross-batch and incremental resolution.
- Add parser, resolver, and ingest discovery regressions.

## Validation
- `cd ix-cli && npm test` (50 files, 649 tests, parser smoke passed)
- `npm run typecheck`
- `npm run build`
- `npm run lint` (0 errors; 38 pre-existing warnings)
- Targeted PHP and resolver tests (36 tests passed)
- Synthetic namespace-based map followed by a caller-only incremental map; all three `CALLS` edges remained attached to existing method nodes

## Checklist
- [x] Tests pass
- [x] Smoke tests pass
- [x] No raw errors introduced
- [x] CLI output follows Ix format

## Release checklist (if merging to main)
- [ ] `ix-cli/package.json` version bumped
- [ ] After merge: tag pushed (`git tag vX.Y.Z && git push origin vX.Y.Z`)
- [ ] If backend changes: `ix-memory-layer` tagged and released first
- [ ] If `docker-compose.standalone.yml` changed: verified `curl | sh` install works

@@ -1025,10 +1025,12 @@ export const PHP_QUERIES = `
 
 ; Method call: $obj->method()
 (member_call_expression
+  object: (_) @_qualifier
   name: (name) @call.name) @call
 
 ; Nullsafe method call: $obj?->method()
 (nullsafe_member_call_expression
+  object: (_) @_qualifier
   name: (name) @call.name) @call
 
 ; Static call: Foo::bar() (php_only uses scoped_call_expression)
@@ -1038,6 +1040,50 @@ export const PHP_QUERIES = `
 ; Constructor call: new User()
 (object_creation_expression (name) @call.name) @call
 
+; Typed properties: private Service $s / private ?Service $s
+;
+; ?Service is NOT a named_type -- tree-sitter-php wraps it as
+; (optional_type (named_type (name))). Matching only named_type silently drops
+; every nullable dependency back to a bare method name, which is most of them in
+; modern PHP. Union types (Service|Repo) are deliberately left out: there is no
+; single receiver type to attribute the call to, so a bare name is the honest
+; answer there.
+(property_declaration
+  type: [(named_type (name) @_typed_var_type)
+         (optional_type (named_type (name) @_typed_var_type))]
+  (property_element
+    name: (variable_name (name) @_typed_var_name))) @_typed_var_scope
+
+; Constructor-promoted properties: private ?Service $service
+(property_promotion_parameter
+  type: [(named_type (name) @_typed_var_type)
+         (optional_type (named_type (name) @_typed_var_type))]
+  name: (variable_name (name) @_typed_var_name)) @_typed_var_scope
+
+; Typed parameters on methods AND plain functions: function run(?Service $s)
+;
+; function_definition is a separate node from method_declaration, so rooting
+; this at method_declaration alone left every top-level function's parameters
+; untyped. The handler needs no change: childForFieldName('name') works on both,
+; and with no enclosing class the scope becomes the bare function name — which is
+; exactly what findEnclosingFunction returns for a top-level function.
+[(method_declaration
+   parameters: (formal_parameters
+     [(simple_parameter
+       type: [(named_type (name) @_typed_param_type)
+              (optional_type (named_type (name) @_typed_param_type))]
+       name: (variable_name (name) @_typed_param_name))
+      (property_promotion_parameter
+       type: [(named_type (name) @_typed_param_type)
+              (optional_type (named_type (name) @_typed_param_type))]
+       name: (variable_name (name) @_typed_param_name))]))
+ (function_definition
+   parameters: (formal_parameters
+     (simple_parameter
+       type: [(named_type (name) @_typed_param_type)
+              (optional_type (named_type (name) @_typed_param_type))]
+       name: (variable_name (name) @_typed_param_name))))] @_typed_param_scope
+
 ; ── Heritage: extends ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 (class_declaration
   name: (name) @heritage.class

commits.message: fix(ingest): resolve PHP calls through typed receivers

fix(php): resolve nullable types and plain-function parameters

The receiver-type queries matched `named_type` only. `?Service` is not one --
tree-sitter-php wraps it as `(optional_type (named_type (name)))` -- so every
nullable dependency fell back to a bare method name. In modern PHP that is most
of them, which made the feature miss the common case rather than an edge one.

Same shape in the parameter query, rooted at `method_declaration`: a top-level
`function run(Service $svc)` is a `function_definition`, a different node, so
its parameters were never typed at all.

Both fixed by accepting `optional_type` alongside `named_type` and alternating
the parameter pattern over both declaration nodes. No handler change was needed
-- `childForFieldName('name')` works on `function_definition`, and with no
enclosing class the scope becomes the bare function name, which is what
`findEnclosingFunction` already returns for one.

Union types are deliberately still bare: a union has no single receiver type to
attribute the call to, so an arbitrary pick of one member would be worse than
the honest fallback. Pinned with a test so it reads as intent, not omission.

Three regression tests; the two for the fixed gaps fail without this change.

comments.body:
Rebased onto `main` — #380 and #384 landed since you opened this, so it was behind.

Authorship is preserved on your commit; only the base moved. Nothing else in the PR was touched, and the review comments above still stand as written.

Pushed the fix from my review as `9c74d47`, since it was the only thing blocking this and it was already written and tested.

**What changed** — only `core-ingestion/src/queries.ts` and `queries.php.test.ts`. Your commit is untouched.

- `property_declaration`, `property_promotion_parameter` and the parameter query now accept `optional_type` alongside `named_type`, so `?Service` resolves.
- The parameter pattern alternates over `[(method_declaration) (function_definition)]`, so top-level functions get typed parameters too.

No handler change was needed, exactly as expected: `childForFieldName('name')` works on `function_definition`, and with no enclosing class the scope falls back to the bare function name — which is what `findEnclosingFunction` already returns for a top-level function.

**Union types stay bare deliberately.** `Service|Repo` has no single receiver type to attribute the call to, so picking one member arbitrarily would be worse than the fallback. I added a test pinning that so it reads as a decision rather than an oversight.

**Verified**
- 3 new tests; the two covering the fixed gaps fail without the query change (`× resolves nullable declared types`, `× resolves typed parameters on plain functions`)
- `queries.php.test.ts` + `resolveEdges.test.ts`: 39 passed (was 36)
- full `ix-cli` suite: 686 passed / 51 files; `npm run typecheck` clean
- `core-ingestion`: 6 failures, the same six you documented as pre-existing on `origin/main` — no new ones

One thing worth flagging for anyone editing this file later: `PHP_QUERIES` is a template literal, so backticks inside those query comments terminate the string. I used them in a first draft and got `Expected ':' but found ';'` from a completely unrelated-looking line. The comments now use plain text.

This clears the blocking review item. The remaining note is the minor one about `.php` joining the prescan set, which is the same incremental-map cost I raised on #375 and is better dealt with there.

reviews.body:
Thanks for contributing! This is careful work — the receiver-type plumbing is well matched to how the existing Python/Go/C++ paths do it, and the `paramTypeMap` scope keys line up correctly with `findEnclosingFunction` (`${className}.${methodName}` on both sides), which is the detail I expected to be wrong and wasn't.

I ran your tests plus a set of probes on your branch. The core mechanism works. Two query gaps are worth closing before this lands, because both are ordinary modern PHP.

## 1. Nullable types silently fall back to bare names

The queries match `type: (named_type (name) @_typed_var_type)`, but `?Service` does not parse as `named_type` — it is `optional_type` wrapping it:

```
private ?Service $s;   → (property_declaration type: (optional_type (named_type (name))) ...)
private Service $s;    → (property_declaration type: (named_type (name)) ...)
```

So on your branch:

```php
class C {
  private ?Service $s;
  public function go(): void { $this->s->create(); }
}
```
resolves to `C.go -> create` rather than `C.go -> Service.create`. Given `?Type` is idiomatic for any nullable dependency, I would expect this to be a large share of real member calls.

## 2. Plain functions are not covered, only methods

The typed-parameter pattern is rooted at `(method_declaration ...)`, so a top-level `function` gets nothing:

```php
function run(Service $svc): void { $svc->create(); }   // → run -> create
```

Your third test pins the bare-name fallback using an *untyped* param, so it passes either way and doesn't catch this.

## Suggested fix — verified on your branch

Accept `optional_type` alongside `named_type`, and alternate the parameter pattern over both declaration forms:

```
; Typed properties: private Service $s / private ?Service $s
(property_declaration
  type: [(named_type (name) @_typed_var_type)
         (optional_type (named_type (name) @_typed_var_type))]
  (property_element
    name: (variable_name (name) @_typed_var_name))) @_typed_var_scope

; Constructor-promoted properties: private ?Service $service
(property_promotion_parameter
  type: [(named_type (name) @_typed_var_type)
         (optional_type (named_type (name) @_typed_var_type))]
  name: (variable_name (name) @_typed_var_name)) @_typed_var_scope

; Typed parameters on methods and plain functions: function run(?Service $s)
[(method_declaration
   parameters: (formal_parameters
     [(simple_parameter
       type: [(named_type (name) @_typed_param_type)
              (optional_type (named_type (name) @_typed_param_type))]
       name: (variable_name (name) @_typed_param_name))
      (property_promotion_parameter
       type: [(named_type (name) @_typed_param_type)
              (optional_type (named_type (name) @_typed_param_type))]
       name: (variable_name (name) @_typed_param_name))]))
 (function_definition
   parameters: (formal_parameters
     (simple_parameter
       type: [(named_type (name) @_typed_param_type)
              (optional_type (named_type (name) @_typed_param_type))]
       name: (variable_name (name) @_typed_param_name))))] @_typed_param_scope
```

No handler changes needed — `childForFieldName('name')` works on `function_definition` too, and with no enclosing class the scope becomes the bare function name, which is exactly what `findEnclosingFunction` returns for a top-level function.

With that applied on your branch:

- `function run(Service $svc)` → `run -> Service.create` ✅
- `private ?Service $s` → `C.go -> Service.create` ✅
- your three PHP tests and `resolveEdges.test.ts` still pass ✅
- full `core-ingestion` suite: 6 failures, the same six you documented as pre-existing on `origin/main` — no new ones ✅

## Deliberately left alone

- **Union types** (`Service|Repo $x`) parse as `union_type` and still fall back to the bare name. That seems right — there is no single receiver type to attribute the call to, so bare is the honest answer. Worth a one-line comment saying so, since the next reader will wonder.
- **Chained and static receivers** (`$this->repo->find()->hydrate()`, `A::make()->run()`, `self::$log->write()`) fall back via `phpReceiverIsSupported = false`. Correct — resolving them needs return-type inference, which is well beyond this PR.

## Minor

`.php` joins the prescan set here, which has the same incremental-map cost I raised on #375 — every unchanged `.php` file gets re-read and re-parsed serially on each `ix map`. The blast radius is much smaller than the JS/TS case in that PR, so I would not block on it, but whatever you land there should probably cover this too.

Happy to re-review once the query is updated.

Blocking item resolved by `9c74d47` — nullable types and plain-function parameters both resolve now, with regression tests that fail without the query change. Verified the full `ix-cli` suite (686) and typecheck clean, and `core-ingestion` still at exactly the six pre-existing failures you documented.

Approving. The remaining prescan-cost note is shared with #375 and belongs there, not here.
